chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abi al-Jawza' al-Munabbih ibn 'Abd Allah, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his forefathers, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:

If a man dies during travel among women, and his wife is not among them, nor any woman among his mahram relatives, he said: “They should wrap him from the waist down to the knees, and pour water over him thoroughly. They must not look at his 'awrah, nor touch him with their hands, and they should purify him. But if women who are his mahram relatives are with him, they should wrap him, pour water over him thoroughly, and touch his body, but they should not touch his private part.”

key_terms.ذَوَاتُ مَحْرَمٍ: women who are his mahram relatives
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a mahram relative with whom marriage is permanently forbidden
key_terms.عَوْرَتِهِ: his private area that must not be looked at
key_terms.يُؤَزِّرْنَهُ: they should cover or wrap his lower body
key_terms.ٱلسَّفَرِ: travel; the circumstance in which this ruling applies

ai.seo_question: How should a deceased man be washed if only women are present during travel?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding the purification of a deceased man when he dies during travel in the presence of women only. It distinguishes between non-mahram women and women who are his mahram relatives, specifying the limits of looking and touching during the washing of the deceased.
